To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Basel III limits the risk of bank runs and the risk of a liquidity crisis, but the central bank can still control the liquidity of the banking system by its unconventional monetary policy.

Basel III limits the tail risk of liquidity stress, in particular if the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) is based on higher quality liquid asset holdings, and that monetary policy conducted via asset purchases gets more leverage on banks relative to policy conducted via refinancing operations.

(1) Basel III limits liquidity risk, (2) unconventional monetary policy is more effective than refinancing operations, (3) the effects of unconventional monetary policy depend on the quality of the bond portfolio, (4) the effects of the bond portfolio depend on the quality and size of the liquid asset portfolio, (5) the effects of liquidity regulation depend on the quality, quantity and composition of the liquid asset and bond portfolio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a macroeconomic liquidity stress testing approach that is consistent with the Basel III standards.
the question whether the combination of Basel III and unconventional monetary policy is able to stabilize the banking system in the event of a financial crisis.
how banks and central banks react to liquidity risks, and how this interaction affects the transmission of monetary policy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liquidity stress testing model shows that Basel III and unconventional monetary policy can work.
the model results indicate that the new Basel III liquidity standards and unconventional monetary policy are complementary and work together.
liquidity regulation and unconventional monetary policy can help to stabilize the financial sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new Basel III liquidity regulation and the unconventional monetary policy of the central bank are complementary instruments.
the Basel III liquidity regulation is a step in the right direction to reduce liquidity risk.
Basel III, in particular if combined with a higher quality of the banks' liquid assets, is an important step to reduce the banks' liquidity risk and to improve the effectiveness of monetary policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liquidity regulation is not a panacea.

the interaction of liquidity regulation, unconventional policy and the financial system's feedback effects is complex and requires a macro stress testing framework to assess the overall effect of policy changes.
the Basel III liquidity regulation can be an efficient tool for central banks to steer banks' liquidity positions.
